findings.fact: Paper connects residual no-op updates with attention saturation and outliers in its settings; this does not establish the cause of Q-RMEA null-label errors.
Clipped softmax stretches/clips probabilities; no subsequent renormalization is specified.
Learned per-token/head sigmoid gates multiply attention output, allowing attenuation.
Authors limit floating-point gain generality and report a clipped-softmax failure on OPT.

paper_reading.transfer_status: Components known; encoder residual/quantization objective differs from frozen-feature Q-RMEA classifier. No selected method.

verdict.mixture_identity: Correct for T>0 valid tokens. With mu=mean(p)>0, alpha=[mu/(mu+EPS)](p/sum(p))+[EPS/(mu+EPS)](1/T); at mu=0, alpha is uniform. EPS therefore prevents general scale invariance, but does not make mu identifiable from alpha over arbitrary p. Given mu, inversion is p_i=T(mu+EPS)alpha_i-EPS. These are known normalization identities, not L5 contributions. The stored-array results support only the reported two-case numerical checks and small smoothing effects.
verdict.source_transfer: The source motivates investigating normalization pressure and no-op behavior, not a theorem that RMEA loses useful support information. Its clipped softmax is not renormalized, and its learned sigmoid gate changes attention-output magnitude during encoder training. Neither is equivalent to the frozen-encoder RMEA classifier setting. A deterministic mass-based multiplier remains near the magnitude-gating family; a different parameterization alone establishes neither substantive novelty nor benefit. Preserve scoped originalL4 and all stopped branches, including the prohibition on gating/coefficient/seed rescue. Keep residual no-op, semantic no_relation, and quantum acceptance distinct.
verdict.native_observability: Unresolved. Constant arbitrary-p rows establish abstract nonidentifiability, but need not be realizable by the actual fixed word-state frame and native rank-one query circuit. For a fixed frame, write p_i=tr(rho A_i), S=sum_i A_i, and B_i=A_i-alpha_i S. The fiber producing an exact observed alpha satisfies tr(rho B_i)=EPS(T alpha_i-1). Mass is identifiable precisely when tr(rho S)/T is constant on this fiber restricted to reachable native pure states. Alpha-only nonidentifiability would still not establish information loss from the complete head, whose utilities depend on inputs.
verdict.next_question: For one already-selected fixed trace and one fixed label row, is mu constant on the native reachable pure-state fiber producing its exact normalized alpha? Use the original word-state frame and unchanged query circuit: either prove constancy or exhibit two reachable pure states satisfying the same normalization constraints but different tr(rho S). This pair-existence test is necessary and sufficient for nonidentifiability on that fiber. The certificate S in span_R{I,B_1,...,B_T} is sufficient for identifiability, but is not generally necessary on the restricted native fiber. A mixed-state relaxation may provide a sufficient constancy certificate; a mixed-state ambiguity is not a native pure-state counterexample, and even unrestricted pure-state ambiguity must satisfy native circuit reachability. Treat stored-array rounding separately from exact equality. This is a bounded observability question, not a proposed method or gate.
limits: Decisive eligibility gap: no native normalization-observability result, and no demonstrated predictive relevance, substantive new rule, or benefit.
The 80 stored rows come from two fixed cases and do not establish population bounds or training behavior.
Small epsilon-floor weights neither prove irrelevance nor establish that support mass is recoverable.
The 40 effects are separate binary measurements, not a joint 40-outcome POVM; their summed responses have no automatic joint-outcome interpretation.
Resolving native observability would answer an information question, not by itself justify architecture selection, reopening stopped mechanisms, or an L5 claim.
